title: Biyaya 10 peanut (UPL Pn 10): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Biyaya 10 peanut: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Biyaya 10 peanut is a peanut variety from IPB UPLB, College, Laguna. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Biyaya 10 is a registered peanut variety, also sold or known as UPL Pn 10. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1992. IPB UPLB, College, Laguna bred it. It takes 98 to 100 days from sowing to harvest, with 1.71 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

items: **Days to harvest:** 98 to 100 days from sowing to harvest.
**Yield:** 1.71 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Biyaya 10 peanut takes 98 to 100 days from sowing to harvest. That is about the average of the 26 peanut varieties with a day count, 101.3 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 1.71 t/ha trails the average of its group, 1.85. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit peanut fields most often: [bacterial wilt](/diseases/bacterial-wilt), [eggplant leafhopper](/pests/eggplant-leafhopper), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [thrips](/pests/thrips). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Where and when to plant Biyaya 10 peanut
Mani needs loose, well drained soil to fill its pods. Pick a variety by seed size for your buyer, and one rated against rust and leaf spot for the wet season.

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is UPL Pn 10 the same as Biyaya 10?
items.a: Yes. UPL Pn 10 is another name for Biyaya 10. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 98 to 100 days from sowing to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 1.71 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Biyaya 10?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
